reviews.review: Very fun. Free to play as it used to be. Lots of content. Pay what you want. Nothing pay-walled

Take a look at my hours. Do you think I'll have something insightful and in depth to say about the game?

No... at least, not past the beginning.

[b]Try it.[/b] If you drop off, that's fair, but [b]do[/b] try it, it's worth checking out how the game feels to play. Even when you're brand new, it feels good, and if that is enough to hook you, then you can make the judgement on whether to keep going with it.

Writing another review because my other one is gone for some reason and my opinion has changed.

Way too much to say to put into a steam review and obviously I'm jaded with the amount of hours I have in this game over the course of going on six years but the gist of it is I played Warframe because of the promise of what it could be and it's an insanely easy game to sink hundreds of mindless hours into grinding my existence away. Over the last few years the devs have failed to deliver any intelligently designed content that doesn't intentionally waste my time or dumb down what complexity there was in the game to begin with.

For example, there used to be a reason to use a different builds on different weapons but for secondary and melee weapons they almost exclusively use the same build because the devs kept nerfing off meta things into the ground so everything is the same bland mediocrity that they apparently see the game as.

ESO is a gamemode where your ability use is restricted by uses in a given time period and it's harsher for your 4 than it is your 1 to give you some arbitrary sense of difficulty. The devs have stated they want to nerf the one frame that's gameplay is based around her 1 because she's too good at that mode. Let me say that again, Saryn is too good at dealing with the arbitrary restrictions of the mode so lets nerf her everywhere.

I could spend days writing more examples of how the recent event wanted you to grind for 4 hours for a maxed common arcane when there is 20 other commons and probably more than 20 of other rarities that cost more time. Or how that recent event didn't work for the first week or so because it was designed so convolutedly that they didn't know what was breaking system to not reward players after a hour long mission with their earned tokens. Or the devs released a near unplayable update due to gamebreaking bugs then went on vacation for 2 weeks, and the aforementioned busted event happens to take place in that spaghetti-code of an update.

All of those event/recent update related examples were fixed eventually, but it just goes to show that the playerbase is supposed to spend the time DE is asking for beta testing consistently buggy and poorly designed systems.

TL/DR because I really need to stop writing before I spend the entire day on this ♥♥♥♥:
The DE that implimented bullet jumping as a replacement for zoren-coptering because they understood players wanted to go fast is not the DE that is working on this game now, and I can't be asked to spend the next 5 years playtesting mediocre to broken updates that want all of my time every day of every week.

Pretty ♥♥♥♥ game for long-term play-ability. They refuse to add endgame, but they did add one of the worst bullet sponge enemies I've ever experienced: the archons. Not worth getting invested in. I come in for major updates, but that's about it.

Duviri edit: What a disappointing expansion. Just an over-glorified new player experienced update with a disjointed story that makes little to no sense, especially if you're new to the game. Hyped for so long, only to fall as flat as possible. Not worth coming back to.
